fns.desc: search_tag()'s loop `for (i = 0; i < len - plen; i++)` has an off-by-one bound: it should be `i <= len - plen` to also check the last valid position where the tag could occupy the final plen bytes of the buffer. As written, if len == plen exactly (or the tag starts at the last legal offset), the loop body never runs for that index and a real match at the buffer's tail is missed. Used by every PEM tag search (BEGIN/END CERTIFICATE, PRIVATE KEY, DH PARAMETERS); low practical impact since real PEM files have trailing content after END markers, but it is a genuine logic defect, not a heuristic judgment call.
